images.title: Three solids, one circle
images.purpose: Shows that a cone, a cylinder and a ball, each of radius 4 cm, all project onto the floor as the same circle.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Three solids in a row above a thin grey floor line, each with the same circle drawn below the line.
images.exact_structure: Top row, evenly spaced: an upright cone, an upright cylinder and a ball, each 8 units wide (radius 4 units), drawn flat with thin dark outlines and filled teal #0072B2. Under each solid its name in small dark text: 'cone', 'cylinder', 'ball'. A thin grey horizontal line across the frame below them (the floor). Under the line, below each solid, one circle of diameter 8 units with a reddish purple #CC79A7 outline and pale fill: 3 circles exactly the same size. From the widest left and right points of each solid, 2 thin dashed grey vertical lines drop to the left and right edges of its circle: 6 dashed lines. Beside the right circle: 'radius 4 cm'. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Different solids can give the same projection, so one projection does not tell us the object.
images.description: Shows that a cone, a cylinder and a ball, each of radius 4 cm, all project onto the floor as the same circle.
images.context: Concept T10.C3; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Cone on its base, upright cylinder and ball, all radius 4 cm, each project to a circle of radius 4 cm.

image_decisions.why: The idea is that different objects share a projection; three solids over identical circles show it at once.
